$comment: PULSAR rules engine. Each rule compares one contract signal with one threshold. Every threshold cites an id in shared/sources.json or explains, in `assumption`, why it is a team placeholder. Rule order is priority: it breaks ties for the countermeasure and the HRP risk. Hazard, HRP-risk and body-system ids are the official ones in shared/hrp.json and the contract. Served by GET /rules and GET /rules/policy.

policy.assumption: Team decision on escalation policy, the mapping from signal to body-twin system and the hazard each rule is filed under; not taken from a NASA source.
description: Status: the most severe status among the triggered rules; GREEN when none triggers. A signal with no value (null) triggers nothing.
Escalation: follows the status (GREEN self-care, AMBER notify the crew, RED notify the flight surgeon).
Affected systems: the union of the body systems of every triggered rule.

HRP risk: among triggered rules that name an official HRP risk, keep the most severe ones and pick the risk most of them name; ties go to the rule listed first. Null when no triggered rule names a risk.
Countermeasure: the one of the most severe triggered rule (the first listed on a tie).
Factors: every triggered rule, most severe first.

rules.assumption: Team placeholder: no labelled posture data exists, so 0.35 is not calibrated. Arm asymmetry is a secondary rule-based camera signal. RED because a one-sided change in movement is for the flight surgeon to judge, not the app. No official HRP risk is about it, so none is named.
rules.message: One arm is moving differently from the other (asymmetry {value}, limit {threshold}).

rules.assumption: Calibrated on RLDD (data/out/fatigue_report.md, 'Where a threshold would sit'): 0.111 is the cut that lets 5 % of the alert 60 s windows of all 24 subjects fire. Out of fold (each subject scored with the others' cut) it fires on 7 % of alert windows and 24 % of the windows of videos their subject called drowsy. The 5 % rate is the team's choice. Self-reported labels, other people's webcams: not validated on the demo camera, and not a clinical PERCLOS cut-off.
rules.message: Eyes closed {value} of the time, above {threshold}.

rules.assumption: Team placeholder until G2 calibrates the fatigue classifier on RLDD/DROZY (uta-rldd, drozy): 0.70 is the alert level proposed for G1 in GOALS.md, not a validated cut-off. RED by team decision: past this level staying awake on task is treated as unsafe, which is for the flight surgeon to judge, not the app.
rules.message: Fatigue score {value}, at or above {threshold}: not safe to stay awake on task.
Slept {value} {unit} in the last 24 h, under {threshold} {unit}: in astronauts this went with slower reactions.

rules.assumption: No sourced cut-off for mean reaction time: basner-2011-pvtb defines a lapse (355 ms or more) but does not use the mean as a metric. 320 ms is a placeholder about halfway between the team's nominal 284 ms and that lapse cut-off.
The 1-5 daily mood scale is a SYNAPSE design choice; treating 2 or less as the point to talk to the crew is a team assumption.
rules.message: Mood {value} out of 5, at or below {threshold}.

rules.assumption: No source yet for a cabin CO2 limit (candidate: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2, not yet in shared/sources.json): 4.0 mmHg is a team placeholder to replace once the source is added. None of the 17 HRP risks covers cabin CO2 (hrp-risks), so no risk is named.

The dose is simulated (CSA widget); csa-radiation gives context, not dose limits. 5 mSv is a demo placeholder, not a radiation limit. No body-twin zone lights up: the official risk is long-term (Radiation-Induced Cancers), not an acute effect the twin could show.
rules.message: Simulated radiation dose {value} {unit}, at or above {threshold} {unit}.
